notable_absence.finding: Nothing on this page (or its analytics-link-setup sibling) states that Enterprise Analytics is a renamed/successor branding for Analytics, or vice versa - unlike analytics:analytics-scope, whose own dataverse-to-scope rename IS explicitly documented ('(Deprecated) The dataverse of the link. Use --scope instead.' on the sibling page). Given there is no promoted (or even extraction-layer, per the full registry digest) concept for 'Enterprise Analytics' anywhere else in this project's 29 rounds, the rebrand's relationship to the pre-existing analytics: vocabulary is asserted nowhere in the source corpus this POC has seen - reconciliation has no page to point to if it wants to link service:enterprise-analytics-service back to service:analytics-service.

cross_component_finding: This page's own OPTIONS section documents a '--get' flag ('Retrieve link details.') and uses it in the EXAMPLES section ('--get --name l1'), but the SYNOPSIS line at the top of the page never lists --get among the bracketed options - only --create/--delete/--edit/--list appear there. That is an internal SYNOPSIS/OPTIONS sync bug on this specific page, distinct from (and additional to) the --link/--name bug found on the sibling analytics-link-setup page - a second independent instance of the same failure mode (reference generated from code faster than the SYNOPSIS block is kept in sync), reinforcing rather than merely repeating the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis.
cross_product_finding: analytics-link-setup and enterprise-analytics-link-setup are genuinely diverged, not a copy-paste-with-rename: the Analytics command exposes ~30 discrete link-type-specific flags (Couchbase/S3/Azure Blob/Azure Data Lake/GCS, each with its own auth-parameter set), while the Enterprise Analytics command collapses the entire link configuration surface into two generic flags, --link-details <json> and --link-details-path <path>, with no --type, --scope, --dataverse, or per-provider auth flags at all. This is a deliberate architecture change (structured-JSON payload replacing per-field flags), not a rename - and it means the EA command cannot yet express anything the older command's --scope (Analytics-scope-qualified links) or --dataverse compatibility path expresses in CLI terms; whatever scope/dataverse addressing EA links use, if any, must travel inside the opaque JSON blob, invisible to this reference page. Whether that makes the EA surface more advanced (schema-flexible) or simply less mature (fewer discoverable options, an undocumented JSON schema) cannot be settled from this page alone.
